problem.title: Technical SEO services for systems that hide or distort pages
problem.body: Technical SEO services begin with stable crawl access, clear indexation signals, dependable rendering, and usable performance. When those systems disagree, teams spend time treating symptoms while important pages remain hard to discover or interpret.

method.title: Prioritise crawl and indexation fixes by evidence
method.intro: The work turns technical findings into an implementation sequence that developers and site owners can inspect.

steps.title: Crawl access and indexation
steps.body: Review crawl paths, robots directives, status codes, canonicals, and sitemap signals around the pages the site needs search engines to find.

steps.title: Architecture and links
steps.body: Trace navigation, internal links, depth, redirects, and duplicate routes to expose weak discovery paths and conflicting destinations.

steps.title: Rendering and data
steps.body: Check whether essential content and structured signals remain available when templates, scripts, and page states are processed.

steps.title: Site speed and verification
steps.body: Identify performance constraints, assign practical fixes, then verify deployed changes against the original evidence rather than assuming implementation worked.

outcome.title: A healthier technical foundation with accountable next actions
outcome.body: Recommendations are grouped by impact, dependency, and owner so the team can plan changes without turning every warning into an equal-priority task.
points: Clear crawl and indexation rules for priority pages
Technical tickets linked to affected templates or URLs
Performance work framed as part of the wider system
Verification criteria for releases and recurring checks

items.question: Does every crawler warning need fixing?
items.answer: No. Findings are prioritised by affected pages, impact, dependency and ownership. A warning without a meaningful consequence should not displace higher-value work.

items.question: Will developers receive implementation detail?
items.answer: Yes. Recommendations identify affected templates or URLs, the reason for the change and a verification criterion for the release.

items.question: Does technical SEO include site speed?
items.answer: Yes, when performance constrains discovery or use. Speed work is assessed as part of the wider rendering and template system rather than as an isolated score.

items.question: How are fixes checked?
items.answer: The relevant crawl, indexation, rendering or performance evidence is collected again after deployment and compared with the original finding.
